citation: Company CVD policy (POL-03 4.4); supports FD&C Act 524B(b)(1) (N31-33-R05)
trigger: A researcher, supplier, the partner hospital, or anyone else reports a vulnerability in WM-1 or the cloud service
deadline: Acknowledge within 3 business days; agree a public disclosure date with the reporter
notify: Reporter; optionally CISA for a coordinated public advisory
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - now, for pre-production units and the cloud service (policy due 2026-10-31)

obligation: Known vulnerabilities disclosed in the premarket submission
citation: FDA premarket cybersecurity guidance (2026-02-03), sections V.A.2 and V.A.4 (nonbinding); FD&C Act 524B(a) (N31-33-R05)
trigger: Any vulnerability found before the 510(k) is submitted, including from the penetration test or this runbook
deadline: In the submission: each known vulnerability with a safety and security risk assessment and its controls; KEV-listed vulnerabilities designed out
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - now, for the planned 510(k)

trigger: A vulnerability or incident that affects the 8 evaluation hubs or the hospital's test network
deadline: Within 72 hours of the company confirming it (contract term), with interim steps
notify: Partner hospital security team and simulation center manager
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - now; contractual, not legal

trigger: Critical vulnerability that could cause uncontrolled risks in the cleared device or a related system
deadline: Make updates and patches available out of cycle as soon as possible (no day count in the statute)
applies_at_this_tier: After clearance - statutory duty for the cleared device; before clearance the same process is used for evaluation units

obligation: Regular-cycle update for known unacceptable vulnerabilities
trigger: Known unacceptable vulnerability that does not cause uncontrolled risk
deadline: On the reasonably justified regular cycle set in the cybersecurity management plan (planned: quarterly)
applies_at_this_tier: After clearance

trigger: A hospital report or other information alleging the device failed to meet its specifications, including a security failure
deadline: Record on receipt; review, evaluate, and investigate (no fixed day count; internal target: complaint opened within 1 business day)
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution

trigger: Information that reasonably suggests a device the company markets may have caused or contributed to a death or serious injury, or malfunctioned in a way likely to do so if it recurred (for example, a compromised hub that changes alarm limits)
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after the company becomes aware
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution (803.50 covers devices the manufacturer markets)

trigger: An MDR reportable event needs remedial action to prevent an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to public health, or FDA asks in writing
deadline: No later than 5 work days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution

trigger: Information not known when the initial MDR was filed
deadline: Within 30 calendar days of receiving the information
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution, if an MDR was filed

trigger: The company initiates a correction or removal (for example a firmware fix) to reduce a risk to health posed by the device or to remedy a violation that may present a risk to health
deadline: Within 10 working days of initiating it (not required if already reported under Part 803 or exempt under 806.1(b))
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution, unless all enforcement-discretion conditions below are met

obligation: Record of a correction or removal not reported
trigger: A correction or removal that is not reportable (for example a routine update for a controlled risk)
deadline: Keep the record with the justification
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: customer communication (FDA enforcement discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Vulnerability assessed as an uncontrolled risk to safety and essential performance, with no known serious adverse events or deaths
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after learning of the vulnerability: tell customers and users, give interim compensating controls, and describe the remediation plan
notify: Hospital customers; the ISAO (copy of the communication)
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution - guidance; ISAO membership due 2026-10-31

obligation: Uncontrolled cybersecurity risk: fix distributed (FDA enforcement discretion condition)
citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), section VII.B (nonbinding)
trigger: Same as above
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 60 days after learning of the vulnerability: fix, validate, and distribute
applies_at_this_tier: After commercial distribution - guidance

citation: FDA postmarket cybersecurity guidance (December 2016), sections VII.B and IX (nonbinding)
trigger: The company communicates with customers about a vulnerability
deadline: Share customer communications with the ISAO; active membership is a condition of the enforcement-discretion path
notify: ISAO that shares medical device vulnerability information
applies_at_this_tier: Membership planned by 2026-10-31 (POAM-006)

obligation: Business associate breach notice to hospitals
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI held in the cloud service for a hospital customer
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (BAAs may set shorter terms)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no PHI today; applies once hospital data enters the cloud service after clearance

trigger: Breach of a system the company maintains for a customer that holds personal information of Florida individuals
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after determining the breach or having reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: No - not until the company maintains personal information for hospital customers

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company-held personal information)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information the company holds about its own workforce (for example payroll or HR records)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
notify: Affected Florida residents (7 employees and any contractors whose data is held)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for workforce data; the 500-person Department of Legal Affairs threshold cannot be reached

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (for example remote contractors)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a non-Florida resident's personal information is affected; apply each state's law

obligation: Contract manufacturer incident notice to the company (inbound)
citation: Quality agreement security terms (planned, POL-02 A.5)
trigger: Security incident at the contract manufacturer affecting firmware images, provisioning files, or test stations
deadline: Within 72 hours (term to be added by 2026-12-31)
notify: Head of Engineering and QA/RA Manager
applies_at_this_tier: Planned - not in the current quality agreement

obligation: MSP incident notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Security incident in the MSP's tools or affecting company systems
deadline: Per contract (no specific term today; request 24 hours at renewal)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft involving company systems
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 hotline before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual; product incidents at customers have limited coverage

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion is involved (POL-03 4.9)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED - not in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. The proposed sector criteria include manufacturers of Class II or III devices; recheck when final and at commercial distribution

obligation: DoD cyber incident reporting for covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company has no defense contracts

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
